reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Calls for binding international AI regulation
themes.definition: Speaker calls for international rules, binding standards, charters or global governance of AI.
themes.inclusion: Include passages demanding binding universal standards, a global charter, or international governance of AI use.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages that only list AI as an investment area without any governance or regulation claim.
themes.boundary_cases: Support for UN-led governance counts here and also in AI_UN_ROLE if a specific UN instrument is named.

examples.quote: We call for the adoption of binding universal standards so as to regulate the use of AI and digital technologies
We propose also the establishment of a global charter for digital governance and ethical artificial intelligence so that human rights are protected in the digital sphere.
We also call for international governance of artificial intelligence in outer space.

themes.label: Global Digital Compact and UN AI efforts
themes.definition: Speaker welcomes or urges implementation of UN instruments on AI, especially the Global Digital Compact and Pact for the Future, or UN efforts on AI governance.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit references to the Global Digital Compact, Pact for the Future or UN efforts to govern AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude generic support for multilateralism that does not connect to AI.
themes.boundary_cases: A passage welcoming the GDC as regulating AI counts even when the main claim is about regulation generally.

examples.quote: my country welcomes the adoption of the Global Digital Compact (see resolution 79/1), which should enable better use of that technological advance
The Global Digital Compact must become a reality.

themes.label: AI risks deepening inequality for Africa
themes.definition: Concern that AI may exacerbate inequalities or leave developing/African countries as mere users rather than decision makers, with calls for inclusion.
themes.inclusion: Include passages warning that AI could widen divides, or demanding developing countries shape AI governance rather than only consume it.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages about economic inequality with no link to AI or digital technology.
themes.boundary_cases: Mentions of 'digital sovereignty' or technology as 'instrument of domination' may also fit AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: these technological advances can also exacerbate existing divides if their development as well as access to them remain unevenly distributed
a governance of AI in which developing countries decide instead of simply being users

themes.label: Technology as instrument of domination
themes.definition: Concern that AI and technological progress could become a tool of domination, with calls for African digital sovereignty.
themes.inclusion: Include passages warning against technological domination or asserting digital sovereignty in the context of AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general sovereignty claims about sanctions or politics without technology link.
themes.boundary_cases: If the passage only speaks of unequal access without domination/sovereignty language, code AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE instead.

examples.quote: Technological progress must not become a new instrument of domination. Africa must also be a center of creativity, innovation, and digital sovereignty.

themes.label: AI as source of hopes and fears
themes.definition: AI explicitly framed as both promising and threatening.
themes.inclusion: Include passages that pair AI's promise with its threats or abuses in the same breath.
themes.exclusion: Exclude purely positive or purely negative mentions.
themes.boundary_cases: Mild hedges ('opportunities ... however divides') count if both sides are explicit.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence holds great promise for our societies, but it can also pose a number of threats and lead to abuses
a source of many hopes and fears

themes.label: AI listed among transformations or investment areas
themes.definition: AI is named in a list of sectors, challenges or transformations without substantive discussion.
themes.inclusion: Include passages where AI appears only as an item in a list (e.g., invest in education, health, AI) or as a brief contextual remark about transformation.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages that develop an argument about AI governance, risk or inclusion.
themes.boundary_cases: A one-sentence descriptive remark that AI is transforming work and education, with no further claim, counts here.

examples.quote: we need to invest massively in education, in health, agriculture, infrastructure, new technologies, artificial intelligence, inter alia.
AI is already transforming knowledge, work, our economies, education and information.

value.rationale: Mostly Francophone African speeches that fold AI into a broader multilateralism/UN reform agenda, typically calling for global or UN-led AI governance and inclusion of developing countries. A minority only list AI among investment areas or transformations.
